conversation.title: Tell me about your experience
conversation.goal: Describe your logistics work and past jobs in order, and say why you want this role.

turns.text: Thanks for coming in today. I'm Priya, and I'd like to hear about your work history. Could you tell me about your last two or three jobs?

Hello Priya. For three years I work as logistics coordinator in a transport company in Brno, I am responsible about planning of trucks and communication with carriers. Before it I worked two years in a warehouse as dispečink assistant.
Thank you, Priya. Tell me more about the coordinator job. How much work did you have each week?

Every week I plan around 60 or 70 transports. Each day I check the orders, I book the trucks with carriers and I control if the drivers are on time. When is some delay, I call the carrier and I inform the customer.
That sounds like a busy week, thank you. When a driver is late, who do you call first?
First I call the driver, to know where he is and what is the problem. If he cannot arrive on time, then I call the carrier dispečink and ask for new time. After it I inform the customer.
Calling the driver first is smart, so you learn the problem quickly. Thank you. Now, why do you want this job?

I want this job because I like to organize things and solve problems fast. In my actual company I have no chance to grow, and your company is bigger, with more international transports. I want to learn more and take more responsibility.
Taking more responsibility is a good reason to move, Priya. Before that, how many trucks did you plan each week, and for how long?

judge.voice: Mostly useful. It started with my experience, in a hiring-manager setting, and the questions about calling the driver first felt like logistics. It took dispečink as a normal word gap and never treated me as Czech, which I liked. "Dispatch assistant" and "current" were right. But the interviewer called me "Priya", which is her own name, and I wrote "Hello Priya" myself. In a real interview that would be funny. It never touched "responsible about" or "I work for three years", which are exactly what I get wrong. "Mission done" showed up while she was still asking, and she repeated the weekly-trucks question. The recap gave me no phrases for Friday. I'd use it again for rehearsal, but I don't fully trust the corrections yet.
